Title: Verify keyword search returns relevant product matches
Preconditions: The Toolshop site is up and running; the catalog contains at least one item whose name includes the word screwdriver
Steps: 1. Open a browser and go to https://practicesoftwaretesting.com; 2. Find the search box located in the top navigation bar; 3. Enter the keyword screwdriver into the box; 4. Trigger the search either by pressing Enter or clicking the magnifying-glass icon; 5. Wait for the results view to render; 6. Confirm the entered keyword appears as the active search term on screen; 7. Confirm that one or more product tiles are displayed; 8. Confirm that at least one of the returned product names actually contains the word screwdriver
ExpectedResult: The active search term reads screwdriver; the result grid contains one or more items; at least one item's name includes screwdriver
EntryCriteria: Search functionality must be reachable; the catalog must already contain a matching screwdriver product
ExitCriteria: The searched keyword is visible on the results page; result count is above zero; a matching product name is present among the results
EdgeCase: Matching should ignore letter case; partial substring matches should count; results page may take extra time to render under slow network conditions

Title: Verify selecting a category narrows down the product list
Preconditions: The Toolshop site loads correctly; at least one top-level category currently has products assigned to it
TestData: Category value pulled from GET /categories (example: Hand Tools)
Steps: 1. Go to https://practicesoftwaretesting.com; 2. Note how many product tiles show up on the unfiltered home catalog; 3. Find the list of categories in the left-hand panel; 4. Select the first top-level category shown; 5. Allow the product listing to refresh; 6. Check that at least one product tile remains after applying the filter; 7. Compare the filtered count against the original unfiltered count and confirm it is equal to or smaller
ExpectedResult: The filtered grid is not empty; the number of items shown after filtering never exceeds the original total
EntryCriteria: Both the storefront and its API must be reachable; the sidebar of categories must render; the chosen category must contain at least one product
ExitCriteria: After clicking the category, the grid still shows results; the filtered total stays within the bounds of the full catalog count
EdgeCase: Categories with zero products are a special case to watch for; some categories nest sub-categories beneath them; on small screens the sidebar might need scrolling to reach

Title: Confirm a cart item can be added and subsequently removed cleanly
Preconditions: UI and backend API both respond normally; the shopping cart starts out empty; there is at least one in-stock, non-rental item available to test with
TestData: A single in-stock, non-rental product chosen at runtime
Steps: 1. Open the product page for any qualifying in-stock, non-rental item; 2. Confirm the product's title renders correctly; 3. Click the Add to cart control; 4. Check that the cart icon's badge counter updates to 1; 5. Open the cart by clicking its icon; 6. Confirm the newly added item appears as a line in the cart table; 7. Find the remove (trash/delete) action tied to that row; 8. Trigger the remove action; 9. Give the page a moment to refresh the cart state; 10. Confirm the item's row has disappeared from the table; 11. Confirm the badge counter now reads 0 or is no longer displayed
ExpectedResult: Item successfully added with badge at 1; row visible in cart; after removal the row disappears and the badge either shows 0 or is hidden
EntryCriteria: Cart must be empty before starting; the product page must load; the Add to cart control must be clickable
ExitCriteria: Cart row no longer present post-removal; badge reflects the updated count; no error banners appear
EdgeCase: Timing mismatch between the delete API response and the badge refresh; some implementations hide the badge instead of showing zero

Title: Confirm ascending price sort orders items correctly
Preconditions: The catalog page is reachable; there are at least two items on display with differing prices
TestData: Sort selection: price,asc (labelled Price: Low to High)
Steps: 1. Navigate to https://practicesoftwaretesting.com; 2. Confirm multiple product cards are showing in the grid; 3. Locate the sort selector in the catalog toolbar; 4. Choose Price: Low to High from its options; 5. Wait for the grid to refresh with the new order; 6. Note the price shown on the very first card; 7. Capture the price of every visible card in the order they appear; 8. Check that each captured price is less than or equal to the one following it; 9. Confirm no later item shows a price lower than an earlier one in the list
ExpectedResult: Every visible price sits in non-decreasing order once the ascending sort is applied
EntryCriteria: Catalog must load; the sort selector must be visible; a minimum of two differently priced products must be present
ExitCriteria: Prices read out in non-decreasing sequence; no card breaks the ascending order relative to the one after it
EdgeCase: Duplicate prices are considered valid ties; currency symbols must be stripped before comparing numerically; rounding/display precision could cause minor confusion

Title: Confirm the product detail view displays accurate name, price and functioning add-to-cart control
Preconditions: UI and API endpoints both respond; there's at least one in-stock, non-rental product to test against
TestData: One randomly chosen in-stock, non-rental product, with name/price fetched via API
Steps: 1. Call the API to fetch an in-stock, non-rental product's id, capturing its name and price; 2. Browse directly to /product/{id} using that id; 3. Wait until the product title renders; 4. Confirm the on-screen title matches the API-reported name exactly; 5. Locate the price display on the page; 6. Strip any currency symbol and read the numeric price value; 7. Confirm this numeric value is above zero; 8. Confirm the Add to cart button is present; 9. Confirm the Add to cart button is clickable, not greyed out
ExpectedResult: Displayed name matches the API value exactly; the numeric price is positive; the Add to cart button shows and is enabled
EntryCriteria: Both UI and API must be reachable; the product route must resolve; stock status for the chosen product must remain unchanged
ExitCriteria: Exact name match confirmed; price is a valid positive number; button is active
EdgeCase: The product name could theoretically change between the API call and the page load; price formatting may vary by currency symbol; the button could be disabled if stock runs out mid-test

Title: Confirm a custom quantity of four carries through correctly to the cart
Preconditions: A product detail page is already open for an in-stock, non-rental item; the quantity box starts at its default value of 1
TestData: Any catalog product; target quantity set to 4
Steps: 1. Open the detail page of any in-stock, non-rental product; 2. Confirm the quantity input starts out at 1; 3. Clear the field and enter 4; 4. Click the Add to cart button; 5. Wait for the navigation cart badge to appear; 6. Confirm the badge now reads 4; 7. Click the cart icon to view the cart contents; 8. Wait for the cart table to finish loading; 9. Find the row corresponding to the added product; 10. Confirm the quantity spinner on that row also reads 4
ExpectedResult: Quantity field defaults to 1; after entering 4 and adding to cart the badge shows 4; the cart row's quantity spinner also shows 4
EntryCriteria: The detail page must be reachable; the quantity input must accept edits; the Add to cart control must be enabled
ExitCriteria: Badge value equals 4; cart row spinner equals 4
EdgeCase: The quantity field could revert on losing focus; some products may enforce a max-stock cap; typing versus using increment arrows may behave differently

Title: Confirm catalog and product pages render within a 3-second budget under simulated Fast 3G
Preconditions: Chrome with DevTools is available; the storefront is reachable; a Fast 3G throttle profile can be selected
TestData: Fast 3G settings: ~1.6 Mbps down, ~750 Kbps up, ~150 ms latency; pass threshold of 3 seconds
Steps: 1. Launch Chrome and open DevTools with F12; 2. Switch to the Network tab; 3. Choose the Fast 3G throttle preset; 4. Load https://practicesoftwaretesting.com; 5. Note the Load figure reported in the Network panel; 6. Confirm this load time is below 3 seconds; 7. Open any in-stock product's detail page; 8. Note its Load figure; 9. Confirm the detail page also loads under 3 seconds; 10. Turn off throttling and reload once more to sanity-check a faster load under normal conditions
ExpectedResult: Both the catalog page and the product detail page complete loading in under 3 seconds while throttled to Fast 3G
EntryCriteria: DevTools must be available in Chrome; the Fast 3G preset must be selectable; the site must be reachable
ExitCriteria: Load times for both pages are captured and logged as Pass or Fail against the 3-second bar
EdgeCase: CDN/edge overhead can add inconsistent latency; a first visit versus a cached reload will differ; variance across CDN nodes is expected

Title: Confirm catalog, detail, and cart screens remain fully usable via keyboard alone
Preconditions: Chrome browser; mouse input disabled for the duration of the test; a disposable test-account is ready
TestData: Keys involved: Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, arrow keys
Steps: 1. Load https://practicesoftwaretesting.com without touching the mouse; 2. Press Tab and confirm the first focusable element shows a visible outline; 3. Continue tabbing through the nav links, confirming each one picks up focus; 4. Tab into the search field, type a keyword, and press Enter, confirming results load; 5. Tab to a product tile and press Enter, confirming the detail page opens; 6. Tab to the Add to cart button and activate it with Enter or Space, confirming the badge count goes up; 7. Tab to the cart icon and press Enter to open the cart; 8. Tab through the cart's row controls, confirming both the quantity spinner and delete button can be reached; 9. Tab to the catalog's sort dropdown and use the arrow keys to change the selection, confirming the grid updates accordingly
ExpectedResult: Every interactive element across the catalog, detail, and cart pages can be reached via Tab; a visible focus indicator is always present; the full flow completes without needing the mouse
EntryCriteria: Storefront must be reachable; testing done in Chrome; no screen reader or other assistive tech running concurrently
ExitCriteria: All three pages verified; any missing focus outline or keyboard trap is logged as a defect; each page marked Pass or Fail individually
EdgeCase: Custom Angular widgets sometimes ignore standard keyboard conventions; arrow-key behavior on the sort dropdown can differ by implementation
